description.narrative: Center for Human Rights (CHR) etablerades 2008 som en självständig akademisk enhet inom Addis Ababa Universitetet (AAU). Centret engagerar sig i multi-disciplinärt Mänsklig Rättighetsarbete inom bl.a. undervisning, forskning och arbete med bl.a. rättshjälp till behövande grupper i samhället. I enlighet med AAU och CHRs 10-års plan avser centret bli ett av Afrikas ledande forskningsinstitut till år 2030. CHR har 12 anställda akademiker, varav de flesta doktorerade. Projektet har tre övergripande målsättningar: 1) Statliga funktioner har stärkt sin kapacitet att respektera de mänskliga rättigheterna och skydda kvinnor, barn, funktionsvarierade, arbetares och migranters rättigheter. 2) Civilsamhällesorganisationer har stärkts i sin roll att främja de mänskliga rättigheterna och i att skydda ovan grupper i samhället. 3) Kvinnor, barn funktionsvarierade, arbetares och migranters mänskliga rättigheter har skyddat

The CHR was founded in 2008 and is a semi-autonomous institution part of the College of Law and Governance Studies - at Addis Ababa University (AAU). The mission of CHR is to promote human rights through multidisciplinary teaching and training, research, and community service. According to the AAU and CHR’s 10-year plan, the centre aspires to be the leading Human Rights Research Centre in Africa by 2030. CHR has 12 employees, most of who are PhD holders. CHR-STRACE II, has three main objectives: i) increase the capacity of state agencies to respect human rights and to protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants ii) Empower civil society organizations to be active actors in human rights promotion and in protecting the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants; and iii) better protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants.

The overarching aim of the project is to ensure the respect of all human rights of all Ethiopians. Project set three interrelated goals: i) Increase the capacity of state agencies to respect human rights and to protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers and migrants ii) Empower civil society organizations to be active actors in human rights promotion and in protecting the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants; and iii) Better protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers and migrants. To contribute to the realization of these goals, the Project will carry out activities that are grouped under three Sub-Projects: a) Multidisciplinary Human Rights Teaching and Training; b) Research, Policy and Practice Collaboration and Diffusion; 3) Community Based Human Rights Promotion and Protection.
The activities in the project includes: i) launching of one new graduate level human rights education program, provide short term specialized training on human rights ii) review existing MA and Ph.D Program iii) produce textbooks for the multidisciplinary teaching of human rights, iv) organize academic conferences, organize policy dialogue forums, promote the multidisciplinary engagement of human rights, train and support community based organizations to engage in human rights promotion and protection, and v) provide legal and related services to members of disadvantaged social groups
